words.ex: 'Edinburgh 26', said the road sign: 26 miles, so about 42 kilometres.
The British commentator said the ball landed thirty yards from the goal, about 27 metres.
The pilot told us we were flying at 35,000 feet, which is more than ten kilometres up.
The carpenter measured the gap with a ruler: just one inch, about two and a half centimetres.
Which pharmacy is nearest to our hotel? We need one quickly.
'Can we walk to the river?' 'Sure, it isn't far, just across the park.'
Nukus is a long way from Tashkent, so most people fly there.
The beach is just ten minutes' walk from our hotel, so we never need a taxi.
'Where can I buy bread?' 'There's a little shop just up the road, next to the car wash.'
The length of the bridge is 300 metres, from one side of the river to the other.
Measure the width of the window from left to right before you buy curtains.
The height of the climbing wall at the sports centre is twelve metres, from the floor to the top.
The divers measured the depth of the lake: forty metres from the surface to the bottom.
'How long is the film?' 'About two hours, so we'll be home by ten.'
The river here is about fifty metres wide, so we crossed it by bridge.
The top shelf is so high that I need a chair to reach it.
Our basketball coach is 1.98 metres tall, so he can touch the hoop without jumping.
The stream was so shallow that we walked across it without getting our knees wet.
The ice on the lake is thick enough to walk on now: about twenty centimetres.
The walls in our flat are so thin that I can hear the neighbours' TV.
Our new school library is huge: it has more than ten thousand books.
After the match we were so hungry that we ordered an enormous pizza and ate it all.
The science museum has a giant model of a human heart that you can walk inside.
The kitten was so tiny that it could sit in a teacup.
The road up to the village is very narrow, so two cars can't pass each other.
Write down all three dimensions of the box, length, width and height, before you order it.
The sign on the bridge said 'Max height 4 m', only four metres, so the lorry couldn't pass under it.
My ruler is 30 cm long: thirty centimetres from end to end.
The rain gauge showed 5 mm, just five millimetres of rain, so the garden was still dry.
Before we set off, I asked the taxi driver how far it was to the airport. 'About twelve kilometres,' he said.
Children who can't swim must stay out of the deep end of the pool.
Little Asal is only four, so she plays in the shallow end, where the water only reaches her waist.
